questions.q: What does Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) actually encrypt?
options: Data at rest — the physical data files, log files, and backups on storage — decrypting pages only as they're read into memory
Data only while it's in transit between the client and the server
Only the columns explicitly marked as sensitive by Data Discovery & Classification
Only backup files, never the live data files
questions.explain: TDE operates below the query engine at the storage layer, which is why it's called transparent — no application change is needed.

questions.q: Does TDE stop a user with legitimate SELECT permission from reading sensitive data?
options: No — TDE protects against someone stealing the physical storage or a backup file directly, not against an authorized, logged-in user simply querying the data
Yes — TDE blocks all SELECT statements on encrypted columns
Yes, but only for columns without a clustered index
TDE has no relationship to SELECT statements at all
questions.explain: That kind of access-based protection is a different problem — dynamic data masking or row-level security, not TDE.

questions.q: What is the difference between service-managed and customer-managed (BYOK) TDE keys?
options: Service-managed keys are handled internally by Azure with no setup; customer-managed (BYOK) keys are stored in the customer's own Azure Key Vault, letting the customer revoke access and disable the database by design
There is no functional difference — both are stored in the same Microsoft-controlled location
Customer-managed keys are only available for on-premises SQL Server, not Azure SQL
Service-managed keys require manual key rotation, while BYOK keys never need rotation
questions.explain: BYOK matters for compliance frameworks requiring the customer, not the cloud provider, to hold ultimate control over the key.

questions.q: What T-SQL query confirms a database's TDE encryption state?
options: SELECT db.name, dek.encryption_state, dek.encryptor_type FROM sys.dm_database_encryption_keys dek JOIN sys.databases db ON dek.database_id = db.database_id;
SELECT * FROM sys.database_audit_specifications;
SELECT * FROM sys.firewall_rules;
EXEC sp_helprotect;
questions.explain: encryption_state = 3 confirms the database is fully encrypted under TDE.

questions.q: Which of the following is TDE explicitly NOT a substitute for, per this lesson?
options: Row-level security, dynamic data masking, and auditing — each solves a different problem TDE was never designed to solve
TLS configuration for client connections only
Backup file storage location
Database Encryption Key rotation
questions.explain: TDE solves exactly one problem — data at rest — and Lessons 32-36 cover the different problems that require different tools.
